text:
### Observed differences

- A10 became much more frequent: in the earlier window it appeared in about 19 in 100 traces (38 of 200), in the later window in about 70 in 100 (140 of 200), with mean occurrences per trace rising from about 0.2 to about 0.8. [OCC003]
- A10's neighbours changed: earlier, A14 led mostly directly to A15 (about 86 in 100 of A14's outgoing transitions, versus about 1 in 100 to A10) and A10 led to A15 in only about 5 in 100 of its outgoing transitions; in the later window A14 led to A10 in about 66 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (A15 about 33 in 100), A10 followed A14 within one step in about 98 in 100 of the observed ordered pairs, and A10 led to A15 in about 85 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, usually within one step. [DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG002]
- A10 now meets activities it previously met rarely: with A14, A15, A20, A22, A23, A24, A25, A26, A31, A32, A47 and A48, joint appearance rose from about 19 in 100 traces to about 70 in 100, and A10 now runs first in most joint appearances (for example A10 before A20 in about 61 in 100 traces versus about 9 in 100 earlier); with A45 and A46, joint appearance rose from about 16 in 100 to about 48 in 100. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]
- The block A20, A22, A23, A24, A25, A26 — whose members always appear together in both windows — previously ran in a fixed order (each cross-pair in one direction in about 97–99 in 100 joint appearances) and now shows mixed or reversed orders (for example A24 before A23 in about 85 in 100 later traces versus about 2 in 100 earlier; A24 before A20 in about 73 in 100 versus about 2 in 100), with distances between members spreading from single fixed gaps to ranges of one to five steps. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, LAG004, LAG006, LAG010, LAG012, LAG017, LAG018]
- Links to A31 and A32 loosened: A31 led almost only to A22 earlier (about 99 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) and now splits between A22 (about 52 in 100) and A24 (about 46 in 100); the distances between A31 or A32 and the block activities spread from one fixed gap to multi-step ranges. [DIR010, LAG008, LAG016, LAG019, LAG021, LAG024, LAG025, LAG028, LAG029]
- A04 and A08 were executed in fewer traces: about 11 in 100 later versus about 21 in 100 earlier (A04), and about 4 in 100 versus about 20 in 100 (A08); A08's outgoing mix also changed, but the later profile rests on only 8 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A10 changed from a rare, loosely connected step into a frequent step with a fixed place: in the earlier window A10 appeared in about 19 in 100 traces, A14 usually led directly to A15, and A10 met the downstream activities in only about 16–19 in 100 traces without a fixed order; in the later window A10 appears in about 70 in 100 traces, typically directly after A14 and before A15, and precedes A20, A22–A26, A31, A32, A45–A48 in the large majority of traces where they co-occur. The support is direct and consistent rather than merely numerous: A10's participation tripled on 200-trace samples (38 versus 140 traces); the successor profiles of A14 (from A15 to A10) and of A10 (onto A15) shifted in matching directions; fourteen relation items and two gap items all move the same way while the partner activities' own presence stayed essentially unchanged, so the shift reflects A10 joining traces rather than the partners disappearing; and with 69 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected without a change, sampling variation cannot account for the evidence as a whole. [OCC003, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG002, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]

The evidence cannot rule out that both windows capture one broader re-routing of the mid-section — at the same time the A20–A26 block mixed or reversed its previously fixed internal order and A04 and A08 declined — rather than a change confined to A10's place; the data show the new behaviour, not what produced it. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, OCC001, OCC002]

Other differences:
- Within the always-co-occurring block A20–A26, the previously fixed sequence (A20/A22/A23 before A24/A25/A26 in about 97–99 in 100 joint appearances) became mixed or reversed (for example A24 before A23 in about 85 in 100 later traces versus about 2 in 100 earlier), and step distances spread from single fixed gaps to ranges — a change in ordering constraints rather than a swap of two activities. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, LAG004, LAG006, LAG010, LAG012, LAG017, LAG018, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009]
- A31 now routes about 46 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A24, which earlier received almost none of them (A22 previously took about 99 in 100), and the distances from A31 and A32 to the block activities spread from fixed single gaps to ranges. [DIR010, LAG008, LAG016, LAG019, LAG021, LAG024, LAG025, LAG028, LAG029]
- A04 and A08 were executed in fewer traces (about 11 and 4 in 100 later, from about 21 and 20 in 100); A08's outgoing profile also changed, but it is based on only 8 later traces. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001]
